summary: instagram-bridge: GET /posts/{shortcode} reads one post with every carousel item, so a shared carousel is no longer one cover image.
details: New resource GET /posts/{shortcode} (design/instagram-adoption/16 §Resources, 17 P12) over instameow's FetchMedia, which is a REST GET of /api/v1/media/{media_id}/info/. The library takes the numeric media id; the shortcode only sets its referer header. So the bridge decodes the shortcode (base64url over the media id, the algorithm instaloader implements) in a new domain.Shortcode value object.

The 200 body is {shortcode, author, caption, taken_at, items:[{kind, url, width, height, duration_seconds?}]}, with no ids and no ok field. Items keep the author's order. A carousel that arrives without its children is refused rather than read as its cover, and a response whose code or pk disagrees with the request is refused, so a wrong decode can never return somebody else's post.

Failures use the new envelope: 400 for a malformed shortcode (checked before the session gate), 404 when Instagram answers 404, 409 for a session that needs a human, 501 for a well-formed shortcode longer than 11 characters (no known decoding), 502 for any other refusal including a status fail inside an HTTP 200, and 503 while the client is rebuilt.

The caption never enters a span, a log line or an envelope. The shortcode appears in the span only as the route pattern: url.path, which otelhttp fills with the raw path, is overwritten with the pattern for this route. The media id is kept out of the upstream span and out of every error text.
limitations: Unmeasured: no live FetchMedia response has been recorded. The fixtures are built from the library's struct tags. The live probe must confirm the shortcode decode, the status a deleted post and a private post Nora does not follow get (FetchMedia drops the body of a non-2xx, so only a 404 reads as not found; a 400 reads as 502), whether carousel_media is populated, and whether video_duration is present.
Shortcodes longer than 11 characters answer 501. They are reported for posts on private accounts, and no decoding for them is known.
Nora's Python side is untouched: post and reel links are not wired to this route yet (17 P12's Nora half).
